items.author: gamebrief.bsky.social
items.context: Do you finish games or sample them? A backlog of 200 isn't a failure, it's a library. What's your rule for deciding a game isn't for you and moving on? #backlog #gaming #steam
items.text: A simple rule that works for a lot of people: give a game two hours. If it hasn't hooked you by then, move on. That also happens to match Steam's refund playtime limit, so you find out early whether it clicks.

items.author: meikuio.bsky.social
items.context:
When you buy a game, which matters more: the lowest price, playing offline, or knowing you can still access it years from now? What would make you choose a physical copy?
image: Editorial illustration of a hand holding an unmarked game cartridge beside a locked glass cabinet with a luminous game tile and a handheld console nearby.
items.text: Access years from now is the one that price can't fix later. DRM-free games, like the ones on GOG, cover a lot of it: you keep the installer, it plays offline, and it doesn't depend on a launcher or an account.

items.author: taylorrrr94.bsky.social
items.context: Should I download Red Dead Redemption 2 for my Steam Deck? 🤔
items.text: Fair question, it's a huge install. Check the Steam Deck compatibility badge on the store page and your free storage first, and an SD card helps if the internal drive is tight.
